source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּהָכִ֞ין מַלְכ֤וּת רְחַבְעָם֙ וּכְחֶזְקָת֔וֹ עָזַ֖ב אֶת־תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was when was established [the] kingdom of Rehoboam and when [he was] strong, he forsook [the] law of Yahweh, and all Israel with him.

en.L: And it happened, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and when he was strong, [that] he abandoned the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all Israel with him.
en.B: When Rehoboam's kingdom was firmly established and he had become strong, he abandoned the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all Israel with him.
en.R: Rehoboam's kingdom became secure, and he grew strong. Then he turned away from the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the people of Israel followed him.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando el reino de Roboam se afirmó y él se hizo fuerte, abandonó la ley {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y todo Israel con él.
es.B: Cuando el reino de Roboam quedó firmemente establecido y él se hizo fuerte, abandonó la ley {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y todo Israel con él.
es.R: El reino de Roboam llegó a estar seguro, y él se hizo fuerte. Entonces se apartó de la ley {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y todo el pueblo de Israel lo siguió.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand le royaume de Roboam fut affermi et quand il fut devenu fort, [qu’]il abandonna la loi {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et tout Israël avec lui.
fr.B: Quand le royaume de Roboam fut bien affermi et qu’il fut devenu fort, il abandonna la loi {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et tout Israël avec lui.
fr.R: Le royaume de Roboam est devenu solide, et Roboam est devenu puissant. Alors il a abandonné la loi {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et tout le peuple d’Israël l’a suivi.

sw.L: Ikawa ufalme wa Rehoboamu ulipoimarika, naye alipokuwa na nguvu, akaiacha sheria ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na Israeli wote pamoja naye.
sw.B: Ufalme wa Rehoboamu ulipoimarika na yeye mwenyewe alipokuwa na nguvu, aliiacha sheria ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na Israeli wote pamoja naye.
sw.R: Ufalme wa Rehoboamu ukawa imara, naye akapata nguvu. Kisha akaiacha sheria ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na watu wote wa Israeli wakamfuata.

vi.L: Xảy ra, khi vương quốc của Rô-bô-am đã được vững lập và khi ông đã mạnh, [thì] ông lìa bỏ luật pháp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên với ông.
vi.B: Khi vương quốc của Rô-bô-am đã vững chắc và ông đã trở nên hùng mạnh, ông lìa bỏ luật pháp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng theo ông.
vi.R: Vương quốc của Rô-bô-am đã vững vàng, và ông trở nên hùng mạnh. Bấy giờ ông quay lưng lìa bỏ luật pháp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng theo ông.

ko.L: 그리고 르호보암의 나라가 굳게 서고 그가 강해졌을 때에, 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 율법을 버렸고, 온 이스라엘도 그와 함께 [버렸다].
ko.B: 르호보암의 나라가 든든히 서고 그가 강해지자, 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 율법을 버렸고, 온 이스라엘도 그를 따라 율법을 버렸다.
ko.R: 르호보암의 나라는 안정되었고, 그는 강해졌다. 그러자 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 율법에서 떠났고, 이스라엘의 모든 백성도 그를 따랐다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando o reino de Roboão foi firmado e quando ele se fortaleceu, ele abandonou a lei {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e todo o Israel com ele.
pt.B: Quando o reino de Roboão ficou bem firmado e ele se tornou forte, ele abandonou a lei {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e todo o Israel com ele.
pt.R: O reino de Roboão ficou seguro, e ele se tornou forte. Então ele abandonou a lei {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e todo o povo de Israel o seguiu.

decisions.choice: he abandoned the law of Yahweh: strength led to unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Chronicles often shows a king who becomes secure and then turns from Yahweh (26:16; 32:25). Rehoboam had begun well: for three years he and the people walked in the way of David and Solomon (11:17). Once his kingdom was firm, he left Yahweh's law. The verb "abandon" returns in Yahweh's answer in verse 5.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the people of Rehoboam's kingdom
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses "Israel" for the people of Judah and Benjamin who stayed with Rehoboam, together with those from the north who joined them (11:3, 13-17). They are the true people of Israel in the writer's view, so the name is kept here; verse 6 calls their leaders "the princes of Israel" in the same way.

decisions.choice: when he was strong: when he had grown powerful
decisions.reason: The second phrase is a noun with "his" ("according to his strength"), here meaning the time when his power was firm. It echoes 11:17, where the Levites and others "strengthened" the kingdom of Judah for three years.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel followed him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the people went the same way as their king, which is what "and all Israel with him" means.

decisions.choice: "la ley del SEÑOR" at every level
decisions.reason: The law (*torah*) is "la ley" at every level here, as the English keeps "law"; the Spanish of 2 Kings says "enseñanza" at Readable only for "the book of the law".

decisions.choice: abandonou (every level)
decisions.reason: "Abandonar" at every level, where the English Readable says "turned away from", so that the reader hears the same verb when the LORD answers in verse 5, "Vocês me abandonaram, por isso eu também abandono vocês" (m1); the plain word serves Readable too.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַֽחֲמִישִׁית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֥י מָעֲל֖וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the year the fifth of King Rehoboam, came up Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem, for they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh,

en.L: And it happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam [that] Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had acted unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: In King Rehoboam's fifth year, because they had broken faith with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem,
en.R: So in the fifth year that Rehoboam was king, Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem. This happened because the people had been unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y sucedió en el año quinto del rey Roboam [que] Sisac, rey de Egipto, subió contra Jerusalén, porque habían sido infieles {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}},
es.B: En el quinto año del rey Roboam, porque habían sido infieles {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, Sisac, rey de Egipto, subió contra Jerusalén,
es.R: Así que en el quinto año del reinado de Roboam, Sisac, el rey de Egipto, atacó Jerusalén. Esto sucedió porque el pueblo había sido infiel {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et il arriva, la cinquième année du roi Roboam, [que] Shishaq, roi d’Égypte, monta contre Jérusalem, parce qu’ils avaient été infidèles envers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}},
fr.B: La cinquième année du règne de Roboam, parce qu’on avait été infidèle {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, Shishaq, roi d’Égypte, monta contre Jérusalem,
fr.R: Alors, pendant la cinquième année du règne de Roboam, Shishaq, le roi d’Égypte, a attaqué Jérusalem. C’est arrivé parce que le peuple avait été infidèle {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Ikawa katika mwaka wa tano wa mfalme Rehoboamu, Shishaki mfalme wa Misri akapanda dhidi ya Yerusalemu, kwa sababu walikuwa wamemkosea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} uaminifu,
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa tano wa mfalme Rehoboamu, kwa sababu walikuwa wamevunja uaminifu wao kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Shishaki mfalme wa Misri alipanda kuushambulia Yerusalemu,
sw.R: Basi katika mwaka wa tano wa utawala wa Rehoboamu, Shishaki, mfalme wa Misri, aliushambulia Yerusalemu. Hilo lilitokea kwa sababu watu walikuwa si waaminifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Xảy ra vào năm thứ năm đời vua Rô-bô-am, Si-sắc vua Ai Cập đi lên đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem, vì họ đã bất trung với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}},
vi.B: Năm thứ năm đời vua Rô-bô-am, vì họ đã bất trung với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nên Si-sắc vua Ai Cập đi lên đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem,
vi.R: Vậy vào năm thứ năm Rô-bô-am làm vua, Si-sắc, vua Ai Cập, tấn công Giê-ru-sa-lem. Việc này xảy ra vì dân chúng đã bất trung với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 르호보암 왕 제5년에 이집트 왕 시삭이 예루살렘을 치러 올라왔다. 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 신실하지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 르호보암 왕이 다스린 지 5년째 되는 해에, 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 신의를 저버렸기 때문에 이집트 왕 시삭이 예루살렘을 치러 올라왔다.
ko.R: 르호보암이 왕이 된 지 5년째 되는 해에 이집트 왕 시삭이 예루살렘을 공격했다. 백성이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 신실하지 않았기 때문에 이런 일이 일어났다.

pt.L: E aconteceu no quinto ano do rei Roboão [que] Sisaque, rei do Egito, subiu contra Jerusalém, porque tinham cometido infidelidade contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}},
pt.B: No quinto ano do rei Roboão, porque tinham sido infiéis {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, Sisaque, rei do Egito, subiu contra Jerusalém,
pt.R: Assim, no quinto ano em que Roboão era rei, Sisaque, o rei do Egito, atacou Jerusalém. Isso aconteceu porque o povo tinha sido infiel {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 14:25, with a reason added
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 14:25 almost word for word (Shishak is the pharaoh Sheshonq I; see the note there). Chronicles adds the reason: "because they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh". Kings only sets the invasion after its list of Judah's sins.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully: broke faith with Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to break trust, as a wife unfaithful to her husband (Numbers 5:12) or one who takes what belongs to Yahweh (Joshua 7:1). Chronicles uses it for the sin that brings disaster on Israel and Judah (1 Chronicles 10:13; 2 Chronicles 36:14).

decisions.choice: they: the king and the people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. It looks back to Rehoboam "and all Israel with him" (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the reason placed before the main clause (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the reason first so that the list of Shishak's forces in verse 3 can follow "came up against Jerusalem" directly, as it does in the Hebrew sentence.

decisions.choice: attacked Jerusalem (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:25: "came up against" means came to attack. Readable names "the people" as those who were unfaithful (m3).

decisions.choice: wording of 1 Kings 14:25 kept; "Sisac"
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 14:25 and adds the reason (meaning decision); Shishak follows the Kings terms note.

decisions.choice: "habían sido infieles"
decisions.reason: The verb is breaking faith, as an unfaithful wife (meaning decision); Spanish "infiel" carries that sense at every level.

decisions.choice: the wording of 1 Kings 14:25, with "vì họ đã bất trung với CHÚA" added
decisions.reason: Chronicles adds the reason (m1, m2); "bất trung" says breaking faith with the LORD and is kept for this verb through Chronicles.

decisions.choice: The wording of 1 Kings 14:21-31 at each level where the Hebrew is the same; "제5년" (L), "5년째 되는 해" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Verses 2, 9-11, 13 and 15-16 retell 1 Kings 14; the Korean repeats Kings there and adds Chronicles' own words, such as the reason given here (m1).

decisions.choice: the wording of 1 Kings 14:25; Sisaque; cometido infidelidade contra (L), sido infiéis (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verse keeps the Portuguese of 1 Kings 14:25 at each level ("Sisaque, rei do Egito", "subiu contra Jerusalém" (L, B), "atacou" (R)) and adds the reason Chronicles gives (m1). The verb of breaking faith (m2) is "infidelidade", "infiéis", as 1 Chronicles 10:13 and 9:1 have it in Portuguese.

source.text: בְּאֶ֤לֶף וּמָאתַ֨יִם֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּבְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֗ר לָעָ֞ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤אוּ עִמּוֹ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לוּבִ֥ים סֻכִּיִּ֖ים וְכוּשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: with thousand and two hundred chariot[s] and with sixty thousand horsemen; and [there was] no number to the people who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

en.L: with 1,200 chariots and with 60,000 horsemen; and [there was] no number to the people who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.
en.B: with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen, and troops beyond counting came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.
en.R: He had 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. He also brought more soldiers from Egypt than anyone could count. They included Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

es.L: con mil doscientos carros y con sesenta mil jinetes; y no [había] número del pueblo que vino con él de Egipto: libios, suquienos y cusitas.
es.B: con 1200 carros y 60 000 jinetes, y con tropas incontables que vinieron con él de Egipto: libios, suquienos y cusitas.
es.R: Tenía 1200 carros y 60 000 jinetes. También trajo de Egipto más soldados de los que nadie podía contar. Entre ellos había libios, suquienos y cusitas.

fr.L: avec 1 200 chars et 60 000 cavaliers ; et [il n’y avait] pas de nombre au peuple qui vint avec lui d’Égypte : Libyens, Soukkiens et Koushites.
fr.B: avec 1 200 chars et 60 000 cavaliers, et des troupes innombrables vinrent avec lui d’Égypte : des Libyens, des Soukkiens et des Koushites.
fr.R: Il avait 1 200 chars et 60 000 cavaliers. Il a aussi amené d’Égypte plus de soldats que personne ne pouvait en compter. Il y avait parmi eux des Libyens, des Soukkiens et des Koushites.

sw.L: akiwa na magari ya vita 1,200 na wapanda farasi 60,000; wala hapakuwa na hesabu ya watu waliokuja pamoja naye kutoka Misri: Walibia, Wasukii na Wakushi.
sw.B: akiwa na magari ya vita 1,200 na wapanda farasi 60,000, na askari wasiohesabika walikuja pamoja naye kutoka Misri: Walibia, Wasukii na Wakushi.
sw.R: Alikuwa na magari ya vita 1,200 na wapanda farasi 60,000. Alileta pia kutoka Misri askari wengi kuliko mtu yeyote angeweza kuhesabu. Miongoni mwao walikuwa Walibia, Wasukii na Wakushi.

vi.L: với 1.200 xe chiến mã và 60.000 kỵ binh; và dân theo ông từ Ai Cập [thì] không đếm được: người Li-by, người Su-ki-im và người Cút.
vi.B: với 1.200 xe chiến mã và 60.000 kỵ binh, cùng vô số quân lính từ Ai Cập theo ông: người Li-by, người Su-ki-im và người Cút.
vi.R: Ông có 1.200 xe chiến mã và 60.000 kỵ binh. Ông cũng đem từ Ai Cập đến rất nhiều binh lính, không ai đếm nổi. Trong số đó có người Li-by, người Su-ki-im và người Cút.

ko.L: 병거 1,200대와 기병 6만 명과 함께였다. 그리고 그와 함께 이집트에서 온 백성, 곧 리비아 사람과 숙 사람과 구스 사람은 셀 수 없었다.
ko.B: 그는 병거 1,200대와 기병 6만 명을 거느렸고, 그와 함께 이집트에서 온 리비아 사람과 숙 사람과 구스 사람 군대는 셀 수 없이 많았다.
ko.R: 그에게는 병거 1,200대와 기병 6만 명이 있었다. 그는 이집트에서 셀 수 없이 많은 군인도 데리고 왔다. 그 가운데에는 리비아 사람과 숙 사람과 구스 사람이 있었다.

pt.L: com mil e duzentos carros e com sessenta mil cavaleiros; e não [havia] número para o povo que veio com ele do Egito: líbios, suquitas e cuxitas.
pt.B: com mil e duzentos carros e sessenta mil cavaleiros, e tropas sem conta vieram com ele do Egito: líbios, suquitas e cuxitas.
pt.R: Ele tinha mil e duzentos carros de guerra e sessenta mil cavaleiros. Também trouxe do Egito mais soldados do que se podia contar. Entre eles havia líbios, suquitas e cuxitas.

decisions.choice: Libyans and Cushites: peoples serving in the Egyptian army
decisions.reason: The Libyans lived west of Egypt; Shishak's own family was of Libyan descent. The Cushites came from the land south of Egypt along the upper Nile. Both served as soldiers in Egypt's armies. 16:8 mentions them again.

decisions.choice: Sukkiim: a people otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: The name appears only here. It may be a group of desert fighters or scouts serving with the Egyptian army, but this is not certain. The name is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen: the size of Shishak's force
decisions.reason: The numbers are given as "thousand" counts, like the army lists of Numbers (see the note at Numbers 1 on the size of such totals). Kings gives no figures. The point is that Judah could not resist such an army.

decisions.choice: no number to the people: too many to count
decisions.reason: "There was no number" is a common way to say a crowd was countless (Judges 6:5; 7:12). "The people" here means the soldiers.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); troops (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "people" means an army in the field, worded as elsewhere in the historical books.

decisions.choice: "libios, suquienos y cusitas"
decisions.reason: The peoples take their usual Spanish forms; the Cushites are "cusitas", the people of Cush, rather than the later name "etíopes".

decisions.choice: numbers in words at Literal ("mil doscientos", "sesenta mil")
decisions.reason: Literal writes round thousands in words, as the Spanish of 1 Kings 10:26 does; Balanced and Readable use figures.

decisions.choice: "le peuple" (L), "des troupes" (B), "des soldats" (R); "Libyens, Soukkiens et Koushites"
decisions.reason: "The people" meaning an army is "le peuple" at Literal and "troupes", "soldats" above it, as in French Samuel and Kings. The peoples keep their Hebrew names in French form; "Koushites" rather than "Éthiopiens", which would point to a later country.

decisions.choice: Walibia, Wasukii, Wakushi
decisions.reason: The peoples take the Swahili "Wa-" prefix for a people, as Wamisri and Wafilisti do; the Sukkiim are not known from elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "dân" (L), "quân lính" (B), "binh lính" (R) for the army; "người Cút" for the Cushites
decisions.reason: "The people" as an army is the ordinary word at Literal and "troops" at Balanced and Readable, as the Samuel terms note. Cush keeps "Cút", as in 2 Kings 19:9.

decisions.choice: "리비아 사람", "숙 사람", "구스 사람"
decisions.reason: Peoples serving in the Egyptian army (m1, m2); "리비아" is the modern name, "숙" follows the Hebrew name.

decisions.choice: líbios, suquitas, cuxitas; mil e duzentos, sessenta mil
decisions.reason: The peoples take Portuguese gentilic forms: "líbios", "cuxitas" for the people of Cush, as 2 Samuel 18:21 has "o cuxita" in Portuguese ("etíopes" would name a modern country), and "suquitas" for the unknown Sukkiim (m2), whose name is kept with the "-itas" ending Portuguese gives such peoples. The numbers are round and written in words.

source.text: וַיִּלְכֹּ֛ד אֶת־עָרֵ֥י הַמְּצֻר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he captured [the] cities of the fortifications which [were] to Judah, and he came as far as Jerusalem.

en.L: And he captured the fortified cities that [belonged] to Judah, and he came as far as Jerusalem.
en.B: He took the fortified cities belonging to Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.
en.R: He captured the walled towns of Judah and came all the way to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y tomó las ciudades fortificadas que [eran] de Judá, y llegó hasta Jerusalén.
es.B: Tomó las ciudades fortificadas de Judá y avanzó hasta Jerusalén.
es.R: Conquistó los pueblos amurallados de Judá y llegó hasta Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et il prit les villes fortes qui [étaient] à Juda, et il vint jusqu’à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Il s’empara des villes fortes de Juda et s’avança jusqu’à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Il a pris les villes fortifiées de Juda et il est arrivé jusqu’à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Akaiteka miji yenye ngome iliyokuwa ya Yuda, akafika mpaka Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Aliiteka miji yenye ngome iliyokuwa ya Yuda, akasonga mbele mpaka Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Aliiteka miji yenye kuta ya Yuda, akafika mpaka Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Ông chiếm các thành kiên cố thuộc về Giu-đa, và đến tận Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Ông chiếm các thành kiên cố của Giu-đa và tiến đến tận Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Ông chiếm các thành có tường bao quanh của Giu-đa và tiến đến tận Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 유다에 속한 요새 성읍들을 점령하고 예루살렘까지 왔다.
ko.B: 그는 유다의 요새 성읍들을 점령하고 예루살렘까지 쳐들어왔다.
ko.R: 그는 성벽으로 둘러싸인 유다의 성읍들을 빼앗고 예루살렘까지 왔다.

pt.L: E ele tomou as cidades fortificadas que [pertenciam] a Judá, e chegou até Jerusalém.
pt.B: Ele tomou as cidades fortificadas de Judá e avançou até Jerusalém.
pt.R: Ele conquistou as cidades de Judá que tinham muralhas e chegou até Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: the fortified cities of Judah: the towns Rehoboam had built up
decisions.reason: Rehoboam had fortified a ring of towns in Judah and stocked them with food, weapons and commanders (11:5-12). They did not stop Shishak. Shishak's own inscription in Egypt lists many towns he attacked in the land.

decisions.choice: walled towns (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for towns strengthened with walls and gates.

source.text: וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ בָּ֣א אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֔ם וְשָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִפְּנֵ֣י שִׁישָׁ֑ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַתֶּם֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וְאַף־אֲנִ֛י עָזַ֥בְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־שִׁישָֽׁק׃

records.literal_gloss: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and [the] princes of Judah who had gathered to Jerusalem from before Shishak, and he said to them, Thus says Yahweh: You have abandoned me, and also I have abandoned you in [the] hand of Shishak.

en.L: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah, who had gathered to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so I also have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak."
en.B: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the officials of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem for fear of Shishak, and said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I have abandoned you to Shishak."
en.R: The prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah. They had gathered in Jerusalem to escape from Shishak. Shemaiah told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so now I have abandoned you to Shishak's power."

es.L: Y vino el profeta Semaías a Roboam y a los príncipes de Judá, que se habían reunido en Jerusalén por causa de Sisac, y les dijo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Ustedes me han abandonado|Vosotros me habéis abandonado}}, y por eso también yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he abandonado en manos de Sisac».
es.B: Entonces el profeta Semaías vino a Roboam y a los jefes de Judá, que se habían reunido en Jerusalén por miedo a Sisac, y les dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: {{plural_you:Ustedes me abandonaron|Vosotros me abandonasteis}}, así que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he abandonado a Sisac».
es.R: El profeta Semaías fue a ver a Roboam y a los líderes de Judá. Se habían reunido en Jerusalén para escapar de Sisac. Semaías les dijo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Ustedes me han abandonado|Vosotros me habéis abandonado}}, así que ahora yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he abandonado al poder de Sisac».

fr.L: Et Shemaya le prophète vint vers Roboam et vers les princes de Juda, qui s’étaient rassemblés à Jérusalem à cause de Shishaq, et il leur dit : « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez abandonné, et moi aussi je vous ai abandonnés aux mains de Shishaq. »
fr.B: Alors le prophète Shemaya vint trouver Roboam et les hauts fonctionnaires de Juda, qui s’étaient réfugiés à Jérusalem par peur de Shishaq, et il leur dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez abandonné, alors moi aussi je vous ai abandonnés à Shishaq. »
fr.R: Le prophète Shemaya est venu voir Roboam et les dirigeants de Juda. Ils s’étaient réunis à Jérusalem pour échapper à Shishaq. Shemaya leur a dit : « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez abandonné, alors maintenant je vous ai abandonnés au pouvoir de Shishaq. »

sw.L: Shemaya nabii akaja kwa Rehoboamu na wakuu wa Yuda, waliokuwa wamekusanyika Yerusalemu kwa sababu ya Shishaki, akawaambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Ninyi mmeniacha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa hiyo {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nami nimewaacha mkononi mwa Shishaki."
sw.B: Kisha Shemaya nabii akaja kwa Rehoboamu na maafisa wa Yuda, waliokuwa wamekusanyika Yerusalemu kwa kumwogopa Shishaki, akawaambia, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Mliniacha, kwa hiyo nimewaacha mkononi mwa Shishaki."
sw.R: Nabii Shemaya akaja kwa Rehoboamu na viongozi wa Yuda. Walikuwa wamekusanyika Yerusalemu ili kujiokoa kutoka kwa Shishaki. Shemaya akawaambia, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Mmeniacha, kwa hiyo sasa nimewaacha chini ya mamlaka ya Shishaki."

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri Sê-ma-gia đến cùng Rô-bô-am và các quan trưởng Giu-đa, là những người đã tụ họp tại Giê-ru-sa-lem vì Si-sắc, và nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Các ngươi đã lìa bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng bỏ các ngươi vào tay Si-sắc."
vi.B: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Sê-ma-gia đến gặp Rô-bô-am và các quan chức Giu-đa, là những người đã tụ họp tại Giê-ru-sa-lem vì sợ Si-sắc, và nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Các ngươi đã lìa bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bỏ các ngươi cho Si-sắc."
vi.R: Nhà tiên tri Sê-ma-gia đến gặp Rô-bô-am và các nhà lãnh đạo Giu-đa. Họ đã tụ họp tại Giê-ru-sa-lem để trốn Si-sắc. Sê-ma-gia nói với họ: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Các ngươi đã lìa bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nên bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bỏ các ngươi cho Si-sắc tùy ý xử."

ko.L: 그리고 예언자 스마야가, 시삭 때문에 예루살렘에 모여 있던 르호보암과 유다의 고관들에게 와서 그들에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하십니다. '너희가 나를 버렸으니, 나도 너희를 버려 시삭의 손에 넘겼다.'"
ko.B: 그때 예언자 스마야가, 시삭이 두려워 예루살렘에 모여 있던 르호보암과 유다의 고관들에게 와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. '너희가 나를 버렸으니, 나도 너희를 버려 시삭에게 넘겼다.'"
ko.R: 예언자 스마야가 르호보암과 유다의 지도자들에게 왔다. 그들은 시삭을 피해 예루살렘에 모여 있었다. 스마야가 그들에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀입니다. '너희가 나를 버렸으니, 이제 나도 너희를 버려 시삭의 손에 넘겼다.'"

pt.L: E Semaías, o profeta, veio a Roboão e aos príncipes de Judá, que tinham se reunido em Jerusalém por causa de Sisaque, e lhes disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} abandonaram, e por isso também eu abandonei vocês na mão de Sisaque."
pt.B: Então o profeta Semaías veio a Roboão e aos oficiais de Judá, que tinham se reunido em Jerusalém por medo de Sisaque, e lhes disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} abandonaram, por isso eu também abandono vocês nas mãos de Sisaque."
pt.R: O profeta Semaías foi falar com Roboão e com os líderes de Judá. Eles tinham se reunido em Jerusalém para escapar de Sisaque. Semaías lhes disse: "É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} abandonaram, por isso agora eu abandono vocês ao poder de Sisaque."

decisions.choice: Shemaiah the prophet: the prophet of 11:2-4
decisions.reason: Shemaiah had earlier brought Yahweh's word that stopped Rehoboam from going to war against the northern tribes (11:2-4; 1 Kings 12:22-24). Kings does not tell of this second message; Chronicles alone records it.

decisions.choice: you have abandoned me, and I have abandoned you: the sentence matches the sin
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice. Rehoboam abandoned Yahweh's law (verse 1), so Yahweh leaves them to Shishak. Chronicles states this rule elsewhere: "If you abandon him, he will abandon you" (1 Chronicles 28:9; 2 Chronicles 15:2; 24:20). The second half has "also I", stressing that Yahweh answers in kind.

decisions.choice: from before Shishak: in flight from him
decisions.reason: The phrase means "away from the face of" Shishak: the leaders had retreated to Jerusalem to escape his advance (verse 4).

decisions.choice: into the hand of Shishak: into his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control. Yahweh hands them over to Shishak, as he handed Israel over to enemies in Judges (Judges 2:14; 6:1).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these court leaders throughout the historical books.

decisions.choice: for fear of Shishak (Balanced); to escape from Shishak (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what "from before Shishak" means (m3).

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L); "jefes" (B); "líderes" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the princes of Judah are its leading men.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on "me"
decisions.reason: The English "Me" for God is the clitic "me" in Spanish, which takes no span, as in the Spanish of Kings.

decisions.choice: "princes" (L); "hauts fonctionnaires" (B); "dirigeants" (R)
decisions.reason: The *sarim* as French Kings has them: "princes" at Literal and "hauts fonctionnaires" at Balanced; Readable says "dirigeants", as the English Readable says "leaders".

decisions.choice: wakuu (Literal); maafisa (Balanced); viongozi (Readable)
decisions.reason: The princes of Judah are the court's leading men, not the king's sons; each level keeps one word for them through the block.

decisions.choice: "các quan trưởng" (L); "các quan chức" (B); "các nhà lãnh đạo" (R)
decisions.reason: One word at each level for the princes (*sarim*) of the court, as the English keeps "princes", "officials", "leaders".

decisions.choice: Shemaiah speaks to the king in 합쇼체 ("말씀하십니다"); the LORD's words inside in 해라체; "고관들" (L, B), "지도자들" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula takes the honorific ending when said to a superior, as in the Korean Kings; the oracle keeps God's own speech level.

decisions.choice: Vocês me abandonaram, por isso eu também abandono vocês (B)
alternatives: Vocês me deixaram, e eu os deixei
decisions.reason: The LORD's sentence matches the sin with the same verb twice (m2), so Portuguese uses "abandonar" in both halves and in verse 1. He speaks to the king and his officials together, so "vocês", with the unstressed "me" under the deity_pronoun setting. Balanced and Readable say "abandono", the present of a sentence being passed now; Literal keeps the Hebrew perfect, "abandonei". "Na mão de" (L) becomes "nas mãos de" (B) and "ao poder de" (R) (m4).

decisions.choice: os príncipes (L); os oficiais (B); os líderes (R)
decisions.reason: The king's officials (sarim) keep the three words 1 Chronicles 19:3 and 28:1 use for them in Portuguese, as the English does (r-en-1); the same in verse 6, where Chronicles calls them "of Israel" (m3).

records.literal_gloss: And humbled themselves [the] princes of Israel and the king, and they said, Righteous [is] Yahweh.

en.L: And the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves, and they said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] righteous."
en.B: Then the officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is righteous," they said.
en.R: Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves. They said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is righteous. He is right to do this."

es.L: Y se humillaron los príncipes de Israel y el rey, y dijeron: «Justo [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: Entonces los jefes de Israel y el rey se humillaron. «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es justo», dijeron.
es.R: Entonces los líderes de Israel y el rey se humillaron. Dijeron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es justo. Tiene razón en hacer esto».

fr.L: Et les princes d’Israël et le roi s’humilièrent, et ils dirent : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] juste. »
fr.B: Alors les hauts fonctionnaires d’Israël et le roi s’humilièrent. « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est juste », dirent-ils.
fr.R: Alors les dirigeants d’Israël et le roi se sont humiliés. Ils ont dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est juste. Il a raison de faire cela. »

sw.L: Wakuu wa Israeli na mfalme wakajinyenyekeza, wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] mwenye haki."
sw.B: Ndipo maafisa wa Israeli na mfalme wakajinyenyekeza, wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwenye haki."
sw.R: Ndipo viongozi wa Israeli na mfalme wakajinyenyekeza. Wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwenye haki. Yuko sawa kufanya hivi."

vi.L: Các quan trưởng Y-sơ-ra-ên và vua hạ mình xuống và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [là] công chính."
vi.B: Bấy giờ các quan chức Y-sơ-ra-ên và vua hạ mình xuống. Họ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là công chính."
vi.R: Bấy giờ các nhà lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên và vua hạ mình xuống. Họ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là công chính. Ngài làm vậy là đúng."

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘의 고관들과 왕이 스스로 낮추고 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 의로우십니다."
ko.B: 그러자 이스라엘의 고관들과 왕이 스스로 낮추며 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 의로우십니다."
ko.R: 그러자 이스라엘의 지도자들과 왕이 겸손해져서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 의로우십니다. 그분께서 이렇게 하시는 것이 옳습니다."

pt.L: E os príncipes de Israel e o rei se humilharam, e disseram: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [é] justo."
pt.B: Então os oficiais de Israel e o rei se humilharam. "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é justo", disseram eles.
pt.R: Então os líderes de Israel e o rei se humilharam. Eles disseram: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é justo. Ele tem razão em fazer isso."

decisions.choice: humbled themselves: the response Yahweh promised to hear
decisions.reason: At the dedication of the temple Yahweh promised, "if my people ... humble themselves and pray ... I will forgive their sin" (7:14). Here the leaders do the first part of it, and verses 7 and 12 show Yahweh answering. Chronicles uses this verb often for a king's turning back (32:26; 33:12, 19, 23; 34:27).

decisions.choice: Yahweh is righteous: his judgment on us is just
decisions.reason: The words admit that Yahweh is in the right and they are in the wrong. Pharaoh said the same after the plague of hail (Exodus 9:27), and so does Jerusalem in its grief (Lamentations 1:18). It is a confession, not only praise.

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: the leaders of Judah
decisions.reason: Verse 5 calls them "the princes of Judah". Chronicles uses "Israel" for Rehoboam's people as the true Israel (verse 1).

decisions.choice: He is right to do this (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds a second sentence to show that the words confess that Yahweh's punishment is just (m2).

decisions.choice: se humilharam; O SENHOR é justo
decisions.reason: "Humilhar-se" is the verb of 1 Kings 21:29 in Portuguese and of God's promise at the dedication of the temple (7:14; m1), kept at every level here and in verses 7 and 12. "O SENHOR é justo" is a confession that he is in the right (m2); Readable adds a second sentence to say so, as the English does.

source.text: וּבִרְא֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י נִכְנָ֔עוּ הָיָה֩ דְבַר־יְהוָ֨האֶל־שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה׀לֵאמֹ֛ר נִכְנְע֖וּ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִיתֵ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם כִּמְעַט֙ לִפְלֵיטָ֔ה וְלֹא־תִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּיַד־שִׁישָֽׁק׃

records.literal_gloss: And when saw Yahweh that they had humbled themselves, came [the] word of Yahweh to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; not I will destroy them, and I will give to them like a little for deliverance, and not will pour out my wrath on Jerusalem by [the] hand of Shishak.

en.L: And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, and I will give them a little deliverance, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will not pour out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves, a word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will grant them some deliverance, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Shemaiah this message: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will rescue them, at least in part. I will not use Shishak to pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on Jerusalem.

es.L: Y cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que se habían humillado, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Semaías, diciendo: «Se han humillado; no los destruiré, y les daré un poco de liberación, y no se derramará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira sobre Jerusalén por mano de Sisac.
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que se habían humillado, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Semaías: «Se han humillado, así que no los destruiré. Les daré alguna liberación, y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira no se derramará sobre Jerusalén por medio de Sisac.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que se habían humillado. Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Semaías este mensaje: «Se han humillado, así que no los destruiré. Los rescataré, al menos en parte. No usaré a Sisac para derramar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo sobre Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’ils s’étaient humiliés, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Shemaya en disant : « Ils se sont humiliés ; je ne les détruirai pas, et je leur donnerai un peu de délivrance, et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur ne se déversera pas sur Jérusalem par la main de Shishaq.
fr.B: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’ils s’étaient humiliés, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Shemaya : « Ils se sont humiliés, je ne les détruirai donc pas. Je leur accorderai quelque délivrance, et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur ne se déversera pas sur Jérusalem par Shishaq.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a vu qu’ils s’étaient humiliés. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné ce message à Shemaya : « Ils se sont humiliés, alors je ne les détruirai pas. Je les sauverai, au moins en partie. Je ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servirai pas de Shishaq pour déverser {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère sur Jérusalem.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba wamejinyenyekeza, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia Shemaya, likisema, "Wamejinyenyekeza; sitawaangamiza, nami nitawapa wokovu kidogo, wala hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} haitamwagwa juu ya Yerusalemu kwa mkono wa Shishaki.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba wamejinyenyekeza, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia Shemaya: "Wamejinyenyekeza, kwa hiyo sitawaangamiza. Nitawapa wokovu kiasi, na hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} haitamwagwa juu ya Yerusalemu kupitia Shishaki.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliona kwamba wamejinyenyekeza. Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampa Shemaya ujumbe huu: "Wamejinyenyekeza, kwa hiyo sitawaangamiza. Nitawaokoa, angalau kwa sehemu. Sitamtumia Shishaki kumwaga hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} juu ya Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy họ đã hạ mình xuống, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Sê-ma-gia rằng: "Họ đã hạ mình xuống; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tiêu diệt họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban cho họ một chút giải cứu, và cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không đổ trên Giê-ru-sa-lem qua tay Si-sắc.
vi.B: Khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy họ đã hạ mình xuống, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Sê-ma-gia: "Họ đã hạ mình xuống, nên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tiêu diệt họ. Ta sẽ cho họ được giải cứu phần nào, và cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không đổ xuống Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Si-sắc.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy họ đã hạ mình xuống. Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Sê-ma-gia sứ điệp này: "Họ đã hạ mình xuống, nên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tiêu diệt họ. Ta sẽ giải cứu họ, ít ra là một phần. Ta sẽ không dùng Si-sắc để đổ cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들이 스스로 낮춘 것을 보셨을 때에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 스마야에게 임하여 말씀하셨다. "그들이 스스로 낮추었으니 내가 그들을 멸하지 않겠다. 내가 그들에게 얼마간의 구원을 주겠다. 그리고 내 분노를 시삭의 손으로 예루살렘에 쏟지 않겠다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들이 스스로 낮춘 것을 보시자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 스마야에게 임했다. "그들이 스스로 낮추었으니 내가 그들을 멸하지 않겠다. 얼마간 그들을 구원해 주겠다. 내가 시삭을 통하여 예루살렘에 내 분노를 쏟지 않겠다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들이 겸손해진 것을 보셨다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 스마야에게 이렇게 말씀하셨다. "그들이 겸손해졌으니 내가 그들을 멸하지 않겠다. 그들을 어느 정도 구해 주겠다. 시삭을 써서 예루살렘에 내 분노를 쏟지는 않겠다.

pt.L: E quando {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} viu que eles tinham se humilhado, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Semaías, dizendo: "Eles se humilharam; não os destruirei, e lhes darei um pouco de livramento, e a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira não se derramará sobre Jerusalém pela mão de Sisaque.
pt.B: Quando {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} viu que eles tinham se humilhado, uma palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Semaías: "Eles se humilharam, por isso não os destruirei. Eu lhes darei algum livramento, e a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira não será derramada sobre Jerusalém por meio de Sisaque.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} viu que eles tinham se humilhado. Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu a Semaías esta mensagem: "Eles se humilharam, por isso não vou destruí-los. Vou livrá-los, pelo menos em parte. Não vou usar Sisaque para derramar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira sobre Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: a little deliverance: a limited rescue
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "a little" (a partial escape) or "in a little while" (deliverance soon). Verse 8 shows that the rescue is only partial: Jerusalem is spared but the people become Shishak's servants, so the sense "a little" fits best. The word for deliverance often means escape from disaster, or the people who escape it (Ezra 9:8, 13).

decisions.choice: I will not destroy them: Yahweh's answer to their humbling
decisions.reason: Yahweh's words repeat theirs: "they have humbled themselves" twice. His anger is held back because they turned, as he promised at 7:14.

decisions.choice: my wrath will not pour out: Yahweh's anger pictured as a liquid
decisions.reason: Anger that is "poured out" is anger let loose in full (34:21, 25; Jeremiah 7:20). Here it is held back from Jerusalem. "By the hand of Shishak" means through Shishak as Yahweh's instrument.

decisions.choice: some deliverance (Balanced); rescue them, at least in part (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how much deliverance is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: I will not use Shishak (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states what "by the hand of Shishak" means (m3).

decisions.choice: "un poco de liberación" (L); "alguna liberación" (B); "al menos en parte" (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a little or soon; verse 8 shows a limited rescue (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "la parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à" (L, B); "le SEIGNEUR a donné ce message à" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's formula for the word of the LORD coming to a prophet, as in French Kings; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "lời CHÚA đến với Sê-ma-gia" (L, B); "CHÚA ban cho Sê-ma-gia sứ điệp này" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula of the terms note at Literal and Balanced; Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: um pouco de livramento (L); algum livramento (B); pelo menos em parte (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the reading "a little" (m1): a partial rescue, as verse 8 shows. "Livramento" is the ordinary Portuguese word for God's rescue of his people. The LORD's words run on into verse 8, where the quotation closes.

records.literal_gloss: But they will become to him for servants, and they will know my service and [the] service of [the] kingdoms of the lands.

en.L: But they will become servants to him, and they will know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."
en.B: Yet they will become his servants, so that they may learn what it is to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and what it is to serve the kingdoms of other lands."
en.R: But they will have to serve him. Then they will learn the difference between serving {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

es.L: Pero serán siervos suyos, para que conozcan {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} servicio y el servicio de los reinos de las tierras».
es.B: Sin embargo, serán sus siervos, para que aprendan lo que es servirme a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y lo que es servir a los reinos de otras tierras».
es.R: Pero tendrán que servirle. Así aprenderán la diferencia entre servirme a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y servir a los reinos de otras tierras».

fr.L: Mais ils deviendront ses serviteurs, et ils connaîtront [ce qu’est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} service et le service des royaumes des pays. »
fr.B: Mais ils deviendront ses serviteurs, afin qu’ils apprennent ce que c’est que de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servir et ce que c’est que de servir les royaumes des autres pays. »
fr.R: Mais ils devront le servir. Alors ils apprendront la différence entre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servir et servir les royaumes des autres pays. »

sw.L: Lakini watakuwa watumishi wake, nao watajua utumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na utumishi wa falme za nchi."
sw.B: Hata hivyo watakuwa watumishi wake, ili wajifunze kunitumikia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nini, na kuzitumikia falme za nchi nyingine ni nini."
sw.R: Lakini watalazimika kumtumikia. Ndipo watajifunza tofauti kati ya kunitumikia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na kuzitumikia falme za nchi nyingine."

vi.L: Nhưng họ sẽ làm đầy tớ cho hắn, và họ sẽ biết việc phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và việc phục vụ các vương quốc của các xứ."
vi.B: Tuy nhiên, họ sẽ phải làm đầy tớ cho hắn, để họ biết phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thế nào và phục vụ các vương quốc nơi các xứ khác là thế nào."
vi.R: Nhưng họ sẽ phải phục vụ hắn. Như vậy họ sẽ biết phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} khác với phục vụ các vương quốc nơi các xứ khác thế nào."

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 그의 종이 될 것이다. 그리고 그들이 나를 섬기는 것과 여러 땅의 나라들을 섬기는 것을 알게 될 것이다."
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 그의 종이 될 것이다. 그래서 나를 섬기는 것과 다른 나라 왕들을 섬기는 것이 어떻게 다른지 알게 될 것이다."
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 시삭을 섬겨야 할 것이다. 그러면 나를 섬기는 것과 다른 나라들을 섬기는 것이 어떻게 다른지 알게 될 것이다."

pt.L: Mas eles serão servos dele, e conhecerão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} serviço e o serviço dos reinos das terras."
pt.B: Mesmo assim, eles se tornarão servos dele, para que aprendam o que é {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servir e o que é servir aos reinos de outras terras."
pt.R: Mas eles vão ter de servir a Sisaque. Então vão aprender a diferença entre servir a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e servir aos reinos de outras terras."

decisions.choice: servants ... my service ... the service of the kingdoms: a wordplay with a lesson
decisions.reason: "Servants" and "service" come from the same Hebrew root. Judah wanted to be free of Yahweh's law (verse 1); now they will serve Shishak and learn by experience how hard serving foreign kings is compared with serving Yahweh. Deuteronomy warned of the same exchange (Deuteronomy 28:47-48).

decisions.choice: become servants to him: become subject to Shishak
decisions.reason: The word for servants here means subjects of a foreign king who must pay tribute, not household slaves. Verse 9 shows what this meant: Shishak carried off the treasures of temple and palace.

decisions.choice: but ... and they will know: a limit, then a purpose
decisions.reason: The first word sets a limit on the rescue promised in verse 7. The second verb tells the purpose of the servitude: so that they will learn.

decisions.choice: servants (every level)
decisions.reason: Literal also has "servants" rather than "slaves", so that the link with "service" stays clear at every level and because the people are subjects, not owned slaves (m2).

decisions.choice: what it is to serve (Balanced); the difference between (Readable); other lands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "know my service and the service of the kingdoms" means (m1). "Other" makes clear that the lands are foreign ones.

decisions.choice: "siervos" ... "servicio" ... "servir"
decisions.reason: "Servants" and "service" share one root (meaning decision); Spanish keeps the play with "siervos", "servicio", "servir" at every level, as the English keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" and "phục vụ" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on "servants" and "service" (m1); as the English, Literal too says "đầy tớ" so that the link with "phục vụ" stays clear.

decisions.choice: "종" and "섬기다" kept together at every level
decisions.reason: The wordplay ties serving Shishak to serving the LORD (m1); Korean keeps one verb for both kinds of service.

decisions.choice: servos (every level); serviço, servir
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1), Literal also says "servos", not "escravos", so that the root shared with "serviço" and "servir" is heard at every level (m1) and because the people become subjects of Shishak, not owned slaves (m2). Readable names Shishak for "him".
